title: What is known about 1RB1LF_0RC0RB_0LD1RB_1LE0LB_0LA1LC_0LB---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LF_0RC0RB_0LD1RB_1LE0LB_0LA1LC_0LB---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state machine halts from blank tape. This page records what is established about it, sorted by what each result rests on. Only a first analysis has been done: the macro rules are not yet known.

The tape is short words: at the left end a stretch (1 0)^n followed by words 1 1 0, 1 1 0 0, 1 0; on the right single 1s separated by one, two or three 0s. Both ends grow like the logarithm of the step count.
verdict: The question is open. No halt in the first 1010 steps (C simulator); the macro configuration and its rules are not yet known.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/tmrun.c runs 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt; at the end the tape holds 255 ones.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 394 cells have been visited and 225 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Where a halt can be
claims.text: A closed tape language of windows of 5 cells (tools/py/bbtools/ctl.py, closure checked by the script, not by Lean) contains every configuration reachable from blank tape, and its only halting configurations have F reading a 1 with F>1 1 1 0 1 0.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/exp
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.093). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.087).

claims.title: The stretch at the left
claims.text: At the left records between 8·107 and 1.9·108 steps the left end reads F>0 (1 0)^n 1^2 0^2 1^2 0 ... with n going 34, 35, ..., 39, then back to 34 and up again: the stretch grows one word per record and is periodically consumed.

claims.title: A doubling map at the left end
claims.text: Read the tape right of the head at the left-end visits in state F as words a = 1100, b = 110, c = 10: it has the form c^s MID b^m c c 0 b^j. Between consecutive visits with the same middle word MID, s grows by 2 and (m, j) becomes (m - j - k, 2j + k) for a constant k of the phase: the total m + j is conserved while j roughly doubles, e.g. (33, 1) → (29, 5) → (21, 13) → (5, 29) with k = 3 between 5.4·107 and 7.2·107 steps. A phase ends when m is too small for the next step; then MID changes (like a counter digit) and a new phase starts with small j. Checked on all 39 such transitions from step 1,158 to 5·109 (24 phases, k from 1 to 23), no exception; only the very first transition (step 636) differs.
claims.where: tmrun 1RB1LF_0RC0RB_0LD1RB_1LE0LB_0LA1LC_0LB--- 5000000000 at F L 5000 | python3 py/phase_check.py, output in py/phase_check_5e9.txt

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The macro configuration family has not been found.

explainer.lede: This machine writes short words of 1s and 0s, and both ends of its tape grow like the logarithm of the step count, the mark of a counter. Its macro rules have not been worked out yet. It has run 10<sup>10</sup> steps without halting.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: Short words
html: At the left end the tape reads F>0 1 0 1 0 ... 1 0 1^2 0^2 1^2 0 1^2 0^2 1^2 0 1 0 1 0 ...: a stretch (1 0)^n followed by the words 1 1 0, 1 1 0 0 and 1 0. On the right the tape is single 1s separated by one, two or three 0s.

The head reaches new cells on the left in groups of four (states F, B, E, A). Between 8·107 and 1.9·108 steps the stretch (1 0)^n goes from 34 words to 39 and then falls back to 34: something at its right end consumes it, like a carry.

sections.heading: A run that doubles
html: Read the tape just right of the head, each time the head is at the left end in state F, as the words a = 1100, b = 110 and c = 10. It always looks like c^s MID b^m c c 0 b^j: a stretch of c's, a middle part MID, a run of m b's, and after c c 0 a second run of j b's.

From one such visit to the next, as long as MID stays the same, the stretch grows by two words and the two runs trade: (m, j) becomes (m - j - k, 2j + k) with a constant k for the phase. The total m + j stays the same while j more than doubles, so a phase lasts only a few visits; for example (33, 1), (29, 5), (21, 13), (5, 29) with k = 3. When m is too small to go on, MID changes, like the next digit of a counter, and a new phase starts with a small j. This held for all 39 transitions seen in 5·109 steps (k between 1 and 23). How MID and k change from phase to phase, and so whether a phase can ever end in the halting pattern, is not known.

sections.heading: Where a halt could happen
html: The machine stops when F reads a 1. A closed tape language with windows of 5 cells, which contains every configuration reachable from blank tape, adds that the five cells right of the head must read 1 1 0 1 0: F>1 1 1 0 1 0.

sections.heading: What is not known
html: Not known: the counter's digits and carry rule, and whether F>1 1 1 0 1 0 can arise.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.093). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.087).
After 109 steps the tape spans 394 cells (289 left of the start, 84 right), with a density of 1s of 0.571.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Counter with a doubling map at the left end (exp/exp; macro rules not yet proved)
summary: A stretch (1 0)^n at the left end that grows and is eaten again, followed by words 1^2 0, 1^2 0^2, 1 0 changing like a counter; words 1 0, 1 0^2, 1 0^3 on the right; no halt in 10^10 steps; at the left end a run of 110 words feeds a second run that doubles, (m, j) -> (m - j - k, 2j + k), phase by phase; macro rules not proved.
